instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 requires that no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.62(11) defines lobbyist as anyone employed/contracted by a principal whose duties include lobbying, so all paid lobbyists must register.

Section 13.695(2) requires any change in name of officer/employee or general area of legislative action disclosed in the statement to be reported in writing to the commission within 10 days; this is the closest analog statutory change-reporting deadline (note: this provision governs agency filings; §13.64(3) requires written notice "before" lobbying in a new area, with no specific day count).

Section 13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless already licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.65 requires authorization "before engaging in lobbying" — so the lobbyist must register/be licensed before any lobbying, i.e., zero days after first lobbying.

The statute requires separate filings: the lobbyist applies for a license under §13.63, the principal files a registration statement under §13.64, and a written authorization under §13.65 links them — these are distinct filings for each party.
Section 13.63(1)(a) lists application requirements (social security number, signature, fee) but does not require submission of a photograph with the license application.

Section 13.621(3) ("Performance of public official duties") exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and employees of the legislature from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency which files a statement under §13.695 and its named officials are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 (except as provided in §13.695), giving state agencies a partial exemption with a separate, lighter reporting regime under §13.695.
